text:
alex: Quick check — we're seeing a handful of 401 spikes from the edge proxy where custom headers (X-Project-ID / X-Org-ID) are missing. Old SDK + some customer CDNs are stripping unknown headers. Question: what do we want the API to do when headers are absent but the API key maps to a different org/project? fallback to org inferred from key (and accept), or reject and surface a clear error so customers fix proxies?
maya: my +1 is for accepting when the API key unambiguously maps to an org and project is optional. Most customers rely on key scoping. But we should log and surface a rate-limited telemetry event so SE can reach out.
chris: nuance — if the API key maps to multiple projects (org-level keys) we can't infer project. In that case we should return 400-ish and include a clear action. Also important for audit: record that headers were missing. We had an incident where proxy dropped headers and we silently used fallback and the tenant owner was confused.
alex: good point. Proposal:
- If X-Project-ID present -> validate against key org -> proceed (200/normal)
- If X-Project-ID missing and API key maps to exactly one default project -> proceed but add a warning header and telemetry
- If X-Project-ID missing and API key ambiguous across projects -> 422 with body explaining "project required or use project-scoped key" (422 so client JSON/contract indicates missing piece)
- If API key invalid -> 401
linh: prefer 409? but i think 422 is fine. also for rotation windows: during key rotation we want a short grace period where old and new keys accepted. That lives in auth service, but API should return a specific error code + machine-friendly error code string so SDKs can auto-retry once they refresh keys.
chris: +1 on machine-friendly error code. Suggest we standardize error payload like:
```
{
  "error": {
    "code": "missing_project_header",
    "message": "X-Project-ID header missing and API key maps to multiple projects",
    "retryable": false
  }
}
```
Add a top-level HTTP header X-Redwood-Warning when we accept fallback: `X-Redwood-Warning: project-inferred-from-key`
ops-bot: deploy-check: auth-service-config v2.14 has "allow_project_inference" flag (default false in prod).
alex: ops-bot note is important — we should not flip default to true. I'll open a PR to the auth service and a patch to SDKs to surface the warning header and to show clearer errors on 422/401.
maya: one more: edge proxy can also normalize headers to lowercase which some of our ingress filters reject (we look for exact header name). Please ensure the header lookup is case-insensitive.
linh: added to auth-service checklist — header lookup will be case-insensitive and tolerant of `x-project`, `x-project-id` variants for a rollout window.
chris: small test plan:
- unit: header absent + key->single-project => accepted + telemetry, check X-Redwood-Warning present
- unit: header absent + key->multi-project => 422 + error.code `missing_project_header`
- e2e: simulate AWS CloudFront stripping X-* headers and confirm behavior

alex: cool. I'll tag @support once PR merges so we can proactively contact affected customers. thanks all :thumbsup!
